title: "Phase 2 — Data Wrangling & EDA"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, message=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(ggplot2)
```

```{r load_data}
framingham <- read_csv(here("data/raw/framingham.csv"))
```

## 1. Data structure

```{r structure}
# Inspect dimensions and column types
glimpse(framingham) 
```

## 2. Missingness profile

```{r missingness}
# Summarise NA counts and proportions per variable
framingham %>% 
  dplyr::summarise(across(everything(), list(na_count = ~sum(is.na(.)), na_pct = ~mean(is.na(.)) * 100))) %>% 
  pivot_longer(
  cols = everything(),
  names_to = c("variable", ".value"),
  names_pattern = "^(.+)_(na_count|na_pct)$") %>% 
  filter(na_count > 0) %>% 
  arrange(desc(na_pct))
```

## 3. Key variable distributions

```{r distributions}
# Visualise distributions of key clinical variables

create_plots <- function(col_name){

dist_plot <- framingham %>% 
  filter(!is.na(.data[[col_name]])) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = .data[[col_name]])) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 1) +
  facet_grid(~PERIOD)

return(dist_plot)
}

col_list <- c("AGE", "SYSBP", "DIABP", "BMI", "TOTCHOL", "HEARTRTE", "GLUCOSE")

plot_list <- map(col_list, create_plots)

for(item in plot_list) {
  print(item)
}
```

## 4. Longitudinal structure check

```{r longitudinal}
# Confirm RANDID and PERIOD structure — how many patients, how many have all 3 periods?
patients <- framingham %>% 
  group_by(PERIOD) %>% 
  summarise(n_patients = n_distinct(RANDID)) %>% 
  mutate(attrition_pct = round((1 - n_patients / first(n_patients)) * 100, 1))

patients
```

## 5. Outcome variable summary

```{r outcomes}
# Summarise the key outcome variables (CVD, DEATH, ANYCHD, etc.)
outcomes <- framingham %>% 
  summarise(across(c(CVD, ANYCHD, DEATH, STROKE, HYPERTEN), list(count = ~sum(. == 1, na.rm = TRUE), pct = ~mean(., na.rm = TRUE)))) %>% 
  pivot_longer(
  cols = everything(),
  names_to = c("variable", ".value"),
  names_pattern = "^(.+)_(count|pct)$") %>% 
  arrange(desc(pct))

outcomes
```
